clinician.final_diagnosis: Severe urticarial rash as the initial symptom of COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities developed a diffuse pruritic urticarial rash 3 days prior to onset of respiratory symptoms (E001). She presented to the emergency department with 1-day duration of shortness of breath and hypoxia (SpO2 84% on room air) requiring supplemental oxygen. Physical examination confirmed widespread erythematous, raised, pruritic urticarial rash on bilateral upper and lower extremities and trunk, sparing palmar/plantar and mucosal surfaces, without vesicles or acral lesions (E003). COVID-19 testing returned positive. Detailed medication history excluded drug-induced urticaria (E006). Laboratory evaluation revealed elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 60.9 mg/L, D-dimer 725 ng/mL) with normal white blood cell count and differential (E005). Chest X-ray showed only left basal atelectasis without consolidation (E005). Treatment included oral loratadine and topical triamcinolone for the rash, and remdesivir for COVID-19 (E007). The urticarial rash completely resolved within 48 hours of treatment initiation (E008), supporting the diagnosis of COVID-19-associated urticaria presenting prior to respiratory symptoms.

COVID-19 infection was confirmed with severe disease manifestations (hypoxia requiring supplemental oxygen, elevated inflammatory markers CRP and D-dimer)
Urticarial rash responded to standard treatment with antihistamines and topical corticosteroids, with complete resolution within 48 hours
Chest X-ray showed minimal findings (left basal atelectasis only) despite significant hypoxia, consistent with COVID-19 presentation
